blockers.message: Batch 5 owner escalation: The inventory and approved scope are met. A proof gap in a published prerequisite reaches the Lax theorem through Banach–Steinhaus and cannot be resolved within these pages. Two local proof clarifications also need repair.

Batch 4 owner escalation: Reviewed all 17 assigned items and both pages against the approved NA-10 design and actual supplier proofs; the current cross-batch dependency list is empty. Two published supplier proofs leave prerequisites used by assigned claims unstated, so owner reconciliation is needed. The findings also identify local proof clarifications for the single repair pass.

Batch 18 owner escalation: The generic convergence claims rely on an external supplier whose proof omits the zero-eigenvalue Jordan-block case. The affected hypotheses include G=0. Richardson also needs a deterministic invalid-status branch.

Batch 20 owner escalation: Both assigned findings are repaired: Simpson exactness now establishes p∈C⁴ before using the Peano kernel, and the convex example uses an explicit Darboux-integrability premise with reflection and endpoint-chord arguments. One outside-batch Smolyak consumer needs owner reconciliation of its degree/node-count notation.

Batch 11 owner escalation: The assigned Box–Muller chain relies on a published square-root supplier whose proof omits a needed Archimedean step. The batch also has page-local repairs listed below; the outside supplier gap requires owner reconciliation.
Batch 13 owner escalation: Worker report requires owner resolution: Repair omitted affected consumers

Batch 19 owner escalation: The local quarter-turn prerequisite repair is present, and the assigned batch and its consumers were rechecked. Escalation is required because the published supplier’s alternating-value claim remains unsupported and is used by consumers outside this batch.

Batch 35 owner escalation: All in-scope repairs are complete. Escalation is required because a published Chebyshev degree supplier has an unclosed induction base used by five direct consumers outside this batch; the assigned RKC consumer now proves the claim locally.
Batch 3 owner escalation: Worker report requires owner resolution: Repair omitted affected consumers

Batch 48 owner escalation: The complete batch and its declared suppliers were reviewed against LIN-QZ. Owner resolution is needed for a published supplier proof gap and an approved-scope/page-requirement mismatch; the local proof and algorithm defects are also identified below.

Batch 33 owner escalation: Assigned repairs and affected consumer checks are complete. Owner action remains for the outside-batch complexity proof update and a wording defect in a published prerequisite proof.

Batch 38 owner escalation: Assigned-source repairs are complete. Escalation remains for the published bounded-direction Poincaré proof’s missing integral prerequisites; the assigned interval instance is proved locally. The earlier flag on thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure:step-3.1 was not retained: Littlewood condition 4 gives E=H∪W, which implies the inclusions used there.

Batch 60 owner escalation: The assigned Schur lemma depends on a published Rouché proof that does not justify two steps as written; owner reconciliation is needed before acceptance. Local repairs are also identified.

Batch 58 owner escalation: The assigned pages and all 12 items were reviewed against OPT1 and plan-spec. The Wolfe existence, angle, Zoutendijk, and vector Newton recurrence arguments check out under their stated hypotheses; the local rate theorem needs the Hessian/Jacobian identification made explicit. Escalation is required for an outside-batch consumer input gap and missing separate algorithm-property proofs under the algorithm review rule. The source arguments were cross-checked against [Nocedal–Wright, Numerical Optimization, §§3.1–3.2, 3.5, 7.1](https://www.math.kent.edu/~reichel/courses/optimization/Numerical_Optimization.pdf) and [Dembo–Eisenstat–Steihaug, §§2–3](https://wiki.math.ntnu.no/_media/tma4180/2018v/inexactnewton.pdf).

Batch 49 owner escalation: All locally repairable proof gaps were addressed within assigned files without changing Statements or Definitions. Escalation remains for an outside-batch uniqueness premise and algorithm-property results that require scope beyond this dispatch; the single local repair round is complete.

Batch 55 owner escalation: Both assigned defects are repaired locally. The assigned CFL proof no longer depends on the published transport results, but their proof gaps remain outside this batch’s write scope and need owner reconciliation.

Batch 65 owner escalation: The whole batch was reviewed. Owner reconciliation is required for an invalid published vector Taylor prerequisite and an out-of-batch RATTLE call that omits its solver backend; local repairs are also identified.

Batch 70 owner escalation: Complete batch review found an unresolved prerequisite gap in the imported Wolfe definition, plus local scope, proof, and trace repairs. The external gap requires owner reconciliation; the local repairs should be handled in one repair pass.

Batch 40 owner escalation: The round-zero findings are resolved, including the L/2 descent estimate and bundle initialization failure branch. This final review found unresolved prerequisite gaps in the poll-angle proof and vector-sum definitions, plus a proof gap in the published finite-Jensen supplier; owner reconciliation is required.

Batch 75 owner escalation: The prior findings are resolved: both stepper definitions now check Newton seed membership, BDF2 names and checks its starting residual bounds, and the termination theorem counts the initial checks. The T06 scope and supplier uses remain sound; the source cross-check is consistent with the local index-one reduction and separate high-index treatment ([Hairer–Wanner, §VI.1](https://isy.gitlab-pages.liu.se/fs/phd-courses/simulation/Papers/HairerWanner_VI_1_clean.pdf); [Atkinson et al., ch. 10, §§10.3–10.4](https://homepage.math.uiowa.edu/~atkinson/papers/NAODE_Book.pdf)). One proof-reference defect remains after the single repair. Since this is the final review, escalate it to the owner.

Batch 82 owner escalation: The full batch, controlling NA-13 design and direct suppliers were reviewed. An outside-batch consumer treats the algebraic product-moment functional as a product-law integral without a factorization prerequisite; this cannot be repaired within batch 82, so it requires owner reconciliation. Other local repairs and an approved-scope omission are also reported.

Batch 89 owner escalation: The full batch and supplier uses were reviewed. A published completed-product Tonelli/Fubini proof has an unresolved prerequisite gap affecting assigned and published consumers; local repairs and one approved-scope addition are also needed.

Batch 96 owner escalation: The order-p gradient item has a material approved-scope gap: it assumes the joint state/adjoint error bound, while the preserved design calls for an order-p approximation result under augmented-method hypotheses. The missing discrete-adjoint estimate needs owner reconciliation; local proof repairs are also recorded.

Batch 81 owner escalation: The repair adds n≥1 to the theorem, matching the current phi suppliers, but the approved batch-81 statement covers every square matrix and the repository defines M₀(C). This excludes an approved case. The smallest missing prerequisite is a definition and convergence case for phi on the unique 0×0 matrix; its series is trivial because all partial sums are the empty matrix. Since this is the final review after the single repair, the owner must reconcile the approved scope or authorize restoring that case. The other batch claims and listed consumer uses check out.
